_comment: The blast-radius ledger: what a change to the foundation invalidated, and how it was cleared.
一份台账，不是一张许可名单。每条记录只回答一件事：这次层 S 的改动动了哪些结论、逐条怎么清的。
`entries` is append-only, like `docs/sphinx/source/foundation-log.rst`: a row is never deleted or
softened. An empty ledger is the honest starting state -- it does not mean nothing ever changed, it
means nothing has been cleared through this mechanism yet.
How `.github/project/blast_gate.py` uses it:
* a changed file under `include/foc/`, `src/` or the SIL instruments triggers a ledger entry when at
least `fan_in_threshold` claim rows rest on it, or when it is listed in `watched`;
* the affected set is RECOMPUTED from `claim-basis.json` (transitive closure) and never taken from
the entry -- a hand-written radius that disagrees with the graph is the failure mode;
* every affected row needs a verdict: `holds` (with a reason), `retest` (with the new number and its
evidence) or `refuted` (with the README level it was downgraded to);
* a `watched` instrument that no claim row mentions must carry `hand_rerun`, because an entry that
adjudicates nothing is an empty ritual;
* only entries touched by the current diff get their radius re-checked: an old entry's radius grows as
the graph grows, and re-litigating it on every later commit would punish the wrong commit.
`watched` is a ratchet: each entry is a layer-S instrument whose change re-bases every SIL number, so
adding one requires a reason in the same commit. Removing one when the file is gone is required, not
optional -- the gate refuses a watch whose file no longer exists.
Known boundary, stated rather than hidden: the graph's edges are compile edges and quoted identifiers, so
it sees a changed implementation and cannot see changed *semantics* behind an unchanged signature. Those
changes are seeded by hand and marked `manual_seed` in the entry.
Known boundary, second half: the trigger needs a diff. In a shallow CI checkout the default base yields
nothing to inspect, and the gate says so in its own output instead of reporting a clean pass as if the
trigger had been checked.
